title: Gift Wrap Roll

drivers.name: 20% off promotion
drivers.evidence: Deeper discount (19.9%) than past promotions (10–30%); one past 20% off week (2024-04-15) had x4.07 lift during Easter, but that week had a holiday. Noise-adjusted past promotion lift is x1.0, but price drop is larger and timing is post-holiday, so moderate uplift.

adjustment.analysis: The 20% off promotion is a strong driver, but past promotions show high noise: noise-adjusted lift is x1.0 despite a median of x1.54. The current price drop (19.9%) exceeds prior discounts, and the target week is post-Mother's Day, a low-sales week. The baseline is 3.5, with 98% ordinary week noise. No strong seasonal signal (Memorial Day effect noise-adjusted x1.0). The classical model’s x1.0 is too low—adjust up for the deeper discount and timing. But uncertainty is high: one past week with similar discount (2024-04-15) had x4.07, but that was during Easter. Shrink toward 1.0. No evidence of post-promo dip (no prior post-Mother’s Day promo).

  shelf price: 4.43 (-19.9% vs regular price 5.53)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 3.5 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 10.2 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 7.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-98% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
